items.text: LEARNING OBJECTIVES

items.label: list_item
items.text: Describe experiments to investigate the effects of changes in the surface area of a solid, the concentration of a solution, the temperature and the use of a catalyst on the rate of a reaction

items.label: list_item
items.text: Describe the effects of changes in the surface area of a solid, the concentration of a solution, the pressure of a gas, the temperature and the use of a catalyst on the rate of a reaction

items.label: list_item
items.text: Explain the effects of changes in the surface area of a solid, the concentration of a solution, the pressure of a gas and the temperature on the rate of a reaction in terms of particle collision theory

items.label: list_item
items.text: Know that a catalyst is a substance that increases the rate of a reaction, but is chemically unchanged at the end of the reaction

items.label: section_header
items.text: EXPERIMENTS TO MEASURE THE RATE OF REACTION

items.label: text
items.text: The rate of a reaction is the speed at which the amount of reactants decreases or the amount of products increases. It is measured as a change in the concentration (or amount) of reactants or products per unit time (per second, per minute etc.).

items.label: formula
items.text: r a t e s a t i o n = \frac { \text {change in concentration, volume or mass} } { \text {time} }
